answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance emerges when each new identity must stake and burn a scarce resource token whose value is tied to real computational work. Imagine a dune of accumulated proof-of-useful-work; only agents that can kindle an ember of verifiable compute across a prism of independent validators gain admission. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs proportional real energy and time, making mass attacks uneconomic while honest agents continue operating.
